slides.title: Should Parcelbird launch its own quick-commerce grocery service in 2027?

paragraphs.text: Should Parcelbird launch its own quick-commerce grocery service in 2027?
Board discussion document, January 2027
Parcelbird
Board (two founders, two investors)
Synthetic benchmark data; all figures from the briefing pack
Executive summary
Parcelbird should not launch Parcelbird Now in 2027: its profit rests on results no site has reached, and the cash does more in the software business
Quick commerce is growing fast, but no operator has made it pay, even at national scale
–	US quick-commerce grocery sales nearly tripled from 2022 to 2025, to $5.1B
–	Zipcart loses $1.90 and QuickBasket $3.40 per order; QuickBasket closed 4 of 11 cities
–	Zipcart's densest city turned positive only with a $3.99 fee, and lost 14% of orders
The founders' plan makes money only on four inputs that beat the best site Parcelbird's software runs
–	At benchmark medians a dark store loses $6.17 per order and needs a $63 basket to break even
–	The plan assumes a $45 basket and 1,800 orders a day; the best site reached $42 and 1,400
–	Each Columbus customer still ordering after three months cost about $173 to win
Even if everything goes to plan, the launch breaks the board's 12-month runway rule
–	The $9.5M the plan needs leaves $2.5M at month 18, about six months of runway
–	At benchmark medians nine stores would lose about $18M a year, more than all the cash
Scaling the software is the better use of the cash, and it serves grocers who want fast delivery
–	Nine late-stage grocers would add $864K of ARR, for hires costing $0.8M a year
–	Return to quick commerce only once a site proves the economics and funding exists

slides.title: In January the board should decline the launch, fund the software plan and set clear tests for any later return

paragraphs.text: 1 Market    2 Economics    3 Cash    4 Alternative
In January the board should decline the launch, fund the software plan and set clear tests for any later return
Decline Parcelbird Now for 2027
Fund the software growth plan
Return only when the evidence changes
▪	Keeps the $12.0M of cash, 30 months of runway at today's burn, for the core business
▪	Avoids sinking $5.4M of capex into stores that are hard to recover
▪	Keeps Parcelbird on the side of the grocers it sells to
▪	Hire 2 engineers and 2 sales staff for about $0.8M a year, in step with signed contracts
▪	Close the 9 late-stage grocers, worth about $864K of ARR
▪	Package fast delivery from existing stores for pipeline grocers
▪	A customer site holds positive contribution after site costs for two straight quarters
▪	Baskets near the $63 break-even, or rider output well above 3.0 orders an hour
▪	Rider minimum-pay rules settled in the cities considering them
▪	Funding available beyond today's cash
